_status: DRAFT, NOT IMPORTED. Algeria is the first of three North Africa countries researched this session (AF/G.9 priority 1) -- Morocco and Tunisia alongside it, Libya researched separately after being retested rather than assumed thin. Researched by a subagent this session against the branch's full Research.1.md discipline; several official Algerian domains (dz.cnr.dz, dgfp.gov.dz) refused or reset direct connections, so some findings rest on Wayback Machine snapshots or news-outlet quotations of Journal Officiel text rather than a direct primary fetch -- flagged inline and in _open_questions. Sitting in src/data/research/ pending Thomas's review, following the established DRAFT-then-import pattern.
_note: Algeria's own CPI documents are explicit about NOT following the frameworks this branch has come to expect: three ONS bulletins spanning 2013-2026 all classify goods and services 'conformément à la classification conseillée par les Nations Unies dans le système de comptabilité nationale de 1970' -- the 1970 UN system of national accounts, not COICOP 2018 and not even SNA 2008. The IMF's own 2025 Article IV report draws the same distinction sharply: Algeria's national accounts WERE rebased in December 2023 to follow the 2008 SNA, but the CPI is a separate ONS product that still runs on 2000-survey weights the IMF itself calls 'severely outdated.' On pensions, the CNR's own 2018 and 2026 revaluation announcements both frame pension increases as presidential/ministerial decisions under a wage-actualisation article (Loi 83-12, Art. 43) rather than a price-indexation formula -- and a named CASNOS official, quoted on the record by a Chatham House research paper, states that a comparable social-insurance benefit (health-insurance reimbursement tariffs) 'has not been updated for almost 40 years,' explicitly invoking inflation as the cause of erosion. A secondary legal-commentary source's claim that the minimum wage (SNMG) is set partly by reference to the CPI could not be corroborated against the primary decree text, which contains no such formula -- reported as an unresolved conflict rather than minted as an edge.

_open_questions.question: The CNR's own site (dz.cnr.dz) and the pension ministry site (dgfp.gov.dz) both refused or reset connections this session. Article 43 of Loi 83-12's full statutory language was read only as quoted secondhand in news reporting of the 2018 and 2026 arrêtés, not directly from the Journal Officiel or CNR's own text.

A private legal-commentary site (legal-doctrine.com) claims the SNMG (minimum wage) is set partly by reference to 'l'indice des prix à la consommation,' but the claim is internally inconsistent (cites 'trois principes' and lists two) and the primary decree (Décret exécutif n° 15-59 du 8 février 2015) contains no such formula in the text this session could access. Worth checking Loi n° 90-11's Article 87 and the 2015 finance law directly.

The ISSA country profile for Algeria (issa.int) blocked direct PDF download (403) both with and without a browser user-agent; its corroborating quote on CNR/CNAS benefit adjustment came through a WebFetch read of the live page only, not independently verified against raw bytes the way the SSA.gov quote was.

reports.title: Indice des Prix à la Consommation
reports.description: Algeria's official monthly Consumer Price Index bulletin. VERIFIED DIRECTLY this session via the May 2026 edition (No. 365), cross-checked against 2012 and 2016 editions for stability of wording. 'L'année de base est 2000 et l'année de référence (100 pour les calculs) est 2001... Formule de calcul de l'indice: I m/2001 = Σi (w i / Σi w i)(p m i / p 2001 i)' (a Laspeyres-type weighted arithmetic mean). Classification is 'proche de celle recommandée (par l'ONU) dans le système de comptabilité nationale de 1970' -- explicitly the 1970 UN system of national accounts, not COICOP 2018. All three editions read (2012, 2016, 2026) were searched in full for 'COICOP', 'Manuel'/'FMI', 'SCN 2008', 'Arabe' and 'Maghreb' -- none appear anywhere.

release_schedule.note: ONS Algeria's own 2025 publication calendar (Calendrier des Publications Année 2025) shows the CPI (IPC) released monthly with roughly a one-month lag: e.g. December 2024 data -> released January 2025; January 2025 -> February 2025; February -> March; March -> April; April -> May; May -> June; June -> July; July -> August; August -> September; September -> October 2025 (all documented rows in that PDF). However, the ONS homepage's latest actual news item (dated 26/7/2026) announces the May 2026 IPC release (matching the corpus's existing IPC_mai2026.pdf), which is a ~2-month lag from the reference month, indicating the cadence has slipped from the nominal 1-month lag seen in the 2025 calendar. No 2026 calendar PDF was found on the site (only 'Calendrier des Publications Année 2025' is linked), so future dates are projected from the most recently observed real cadence (2-month lag) rather than taken from a published 2026 calendar.

reports.title: Enquête sur les Dépenses de Consommation des Ménages (2000)
reports.description: The household consumption-expenditure survey ('un sondage auprès d'un échantillon de 12150 ménages réparti sur l'ensemble du territoire National selon 7 strates') whose year-2000 expenditure data underlie the CPI's variety weights, still unchanged as of the May 2026 CPI release -- corroborated by the IMF's own 2025 Article IV assessment ('CPI weights are based on a 2000 household survey and severely outdated, which could lead to errors in the measurement of inflation').

reports.title: Arrêté portant revalorisation des pensions et allocations de retraite
reports.publisher: Ministère du Travail, de l'Emploi et de la Sécurité Sociale / Caisse Nationale des Retraites (CNR), Algeria
reports.description: Annual ministerial order revaluing CNR old-age pensions under Article 43 of Loi 83-12 du 2 juillet 1983. VERIFIED via news reporting of the Journal Officiel text (direct CNR/JORT access blocked this session -- see _open_questions). The 2018 arrêté set tiered fixed percentages by pension-amount bracket (5% below 20,000 DA down to 0.5% at or above 80,000 DA); the 2026 CNR Director-General confirmed the pattern continues, framing it explicitly as 'application des instructions du président de la République... conformément aux dispositions de l'article 43 de la loi 83-12 relative à l'actualisation des salaires servant de base au calcul de la pension' -- an administrative wage-base updating mechanism, not a CPI formula. Corroborated by the SSA/ISSA country profile: 'Benefits are adjusted annually on May 1 by ministerial decree.'
reports.cadence_note: An annual ministerial order, typically taking effect May 1.

reports.title: Décret exécutif n° 15-59 du 18 Rabie Ethani 1436 correspondant au 8 février 2015 fixant les éléments constitutifs du salaire national minimum garanti
reports.publisher: Journal Officiel de la République Algérienne / Premier ministre
reports.description: VERIFIED DIRECTLY this session (Journal Officiel N° 08, hosted via ILO NATLEX). Issued under Article 87 of Loi n° 90-11 du 21 avril 1990, the decree's three articles define only which pay components count toward the SNMG (national guaranteed minimum wage) -- base salary plus certain bonuses, excluding others. Searched in full for 'indice des prix', 'inflation', 'coût de la vie': none appear. Contradicts a private legal-commentary site's claim (unresolved, see _open_questions) that the SNMG is set partly by reference to the CPI.

reports.title: Algeria: 2025 Article IV Consultation-Press Release; Staff Report
reports.description: IMF Country Report No. 25/270. VERIFIED DIRECTLY this session. Annex XI ('Data Issues') states Algeria's CPI weights are 'based on a 2000 household survey and severely outdated, which could lead to errors in the measurement of inflation,' while separately confirming Algeria's national accounts (a distinct ONS product) 'have been rebased in December 2023 with 2001 as a base year, and now follow the 2008 SNA recommendations.' Also states: 'Algeria participates in the Enhanced General Data Dissemination (e-GDDS) and first posted its metadata in April 2009 but is yet to disseminate the data recommend[ed] under the e-GDDS.'

dependencies.basis: ONS, IPC bulletin May 2026, p.8: 'Les pondérations des variétés sont calculées à partir des dépenses annuelles en 2000, données par l'enquête nationale sur la consommation des ménages.'

IMF Country Report No. 25/270, Annex XI Table 2: 'Algeria participates in the Enhanced General Data Dissemination (e-GDDS) and first posted its metadata in April 2009 but is yet to disseminate the data recommend[ed] under the e-GDDS.' Graded as the weaker 'cites' relationship rather than 'methodology_depends_on' because this is the IMF's own classification of Algeria's general statistical dissemination practice, not a claim made by ONS's own CPI documents, and the IMF itself notes Algeria has not fully implemented what e-GDDS recommends.

_dropped.why: ONS's own IPC bulletins (2013, 2016, 2026 editions) state the classification is 'proche de celle recommandée (par l'ONU) dans le système de comptabilité nationale de 1970' -- an explicitly older, different classification vintage than COICOP 2018. No ONS CPI document mentions COICOP anywhere.

IMF Country Report 25/270 confirms it is Algeria's national accounts, not the CPI, that were rebased in Dec. 2023 to follow 2008 SNA. The CPI's own classification remains tied to the 1970 system of national accounts through the May 2026 release.
Full-text search of the ONS CPI methodology documents (2012, 2016, 2026 editions) for 'Manuel', 'FMI', 'IMF' found no reference to the IMF CPI Manual anywhere.

_dropped.edge: dz-ons-ipc-monthly cites an Arab/Maghreb regional statistical body
_dropped.why: No ONS CPI document accessed this session mentions AITRS/AITSR, the Arab Monetary Fund, or the Union du Maghreb Arabe. No new regional node is proposed.

Both the 2018 arrêté and the 2026 CNR statement frame the revaluation as a fixed, tiered percentage set by ministerial arrêté 'en application des instructions du président de la République', under Article 43 of Loi 83-12 (which governs updating of the wage base used in the pension formula, not indexation of the pension payment to a price index). No document ties the percentage to CPI/inflation. Corroborated by SSA's SSPTW Algeria profile: 'Benefits are adjusted annually on May 1 by ministerial decree.'

_dropped.edge: CASNOS/CNAS health-insurance reimbursement tariffs indexed to CPI
_dropped.why: A named CASNOS official, quoted on the record by a Chatham House research paper, states reimbursement tariffs have 'not been updated for almost 40 years' and that 'with the rate of inflation experienced by the country during this long period... the level of reimbursement is insignificant' -- an explicit admission of erosion with no adjustment mechanism, CPI-based or otherwise. Corroborated by an academic paper hosted on cnese.dz (Algeria's own National Economic, Social and Environmental Council site) citing medical-procedure reimbursement 'sur la base des tarifs de 1987'.

The primary decree (Décret exécutif n° 15-59, Journal Officiel N° 08) contains no CPI/inflation reference anywhere in its text -- it only defines which pay components count toward the SNMG. A secondary legal-commentary site (legal-doctrine.com) claims the SNMG is set per 'l'indice des prix à la consommation' among 'trois principes' but the claim is internally inconsistent (lists only two) and unsupported by the primary decree text accessed this session. Reported as an unresolved conflict, not asserted as a real edge.
